s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive night blindness with peripheral vision loss
salient_findings: Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Normal color vision
Few yellow spots on fundus examination
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Flat rod electroretinogram
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence in superotemporal zones
Narrow hyperfluorescent ring inside on fundus autofluorescence
Central macula appears unremarkable on fundus autofluorescence
Supernormal thickness in perifoveal region on OCT
Marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas on OCT
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region on OCT

shortlist.label: Goldman-Favre Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches night blindness since childhood, abnormal ERG, and specific fundus findings

shortlist.label: Congenital Stationary Night Blindness
shortlist.why_kept: Explains night blindness since childhood with normal visual acuity and color vision

shortlist.label: Enhanced S-cone syndrome (ESCS)
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain night blindness and specific ERG findings, although less common

shortlist.label: Retinitis Pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: A possible cause of progressive night blindness, but typically with more severe visual impairment

shortlist.label: Oguchi Disease
shortlist.why_kept: A rare cause of night blindness, with characteristic fundus findings, but less likely given other clinical features

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and specific findings on electroretinogram (large, slow scotopic and photopic responses, flat rod electroretinogram), along with the characteristic fundus appearance and OCT findings, are most consistent with Goldman-Favre Syndrome.

rejected.label: Congenital Stationary Night Blindness
rejected.why: Lack of progression does not fit with the decreasing ERG amplitudes over time

rejected.label: Enhanced S-cone syndrome (ESCS)
rejected.why: Typically presents with more significant visual acuity loss and different ERG patterns

rejected.label: Retinitis Pigmentosa
rejected.why: Usually associated with pigmentary degeneration on fundus examination, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Oguchi Disease
rejected.why: Characterized by a golden sheep-like appearance of the fundus that changes to normal after dark adaptation, not described in this patient
